title: Bike stem 1: the base sketch and the size
summary: Sketch the stem's side on the XZ plane: a 21 mm hole on the X axis and a symmetric outline 47 mm high. A variable size drives the hole's place and the front length. Pad it 22 mm.

steps.say: Push **{PartDesign_NewSketch|New Sketch}**. Select the XZ plane in the list. Push **OK**.
steps.why: The side of the stem lies on the XZ plane.
hints: Find the sketch button in the Part Design toolbar.
The list shows the three planes of the body.

steps.say: Push **{Sketcher_CreateCircle|Create circle}**. Put the centre of the circle on the red horizontal axis. Draw the circle.
steps.why: The axis holds the centre, so the circle only slides along it.
hints: Find the circle tool in the Sketcher toolbar.
Click on the red axis for the centre. Click again for the size.

steps.say: Select the circle. Push **{Sketcher_ConstrainDiameter|Constrain diameter}**. Set the diameter to 21 mm. Push **OK**.
hints: Find the diameter tool among the red constraint tools.
The dialog asks for the diameter of the circle.

steps.say: Push **{Sketcher_CreatePolyline|Create polyline}**. Start on the green vertical axis. Draw a closed outline of four lines around the circle.
steps.why: FreeCAD adds horizontal and vertical constraints as you draw.
hints: Click each corner. Click the first point again to close the outline.
Keep each line horizontal or vertical. Look for the small red sign.

steps.say: Select the two end points of the rear line. Select the red horizontal axis. Push **{Sketcher_ConstrainSymmetric|Constrain symmetric}**.
steps.why: The outline is now the same above and below the axis.
hints: Hold Ctrl to select more than one item.
The rear line is the vertical line farther from the circle.

steps.say: Select the rear line. Push **{Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceY|Constrain vertical distance}**. Set the height to 47 mm. Push **OK**.
hints: Find the vertical distance tool among the red constraint tools.
The dialog asks for the length of the line.

steps.say: Select the rear line and the green vertical axis. Push **{Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceX|Constrain horizontal distance}**. Set it to 27 mm. Push **OK**.
steps.why: This is the length of the rear part of the stem.
hints: The rear line is the vertical line farther from the circle.
Hold Ctrl to select the axis as the second item.

steps.say: Select the centre of the circle and the green vertical axis. Push **{Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceX|Constrain horizontal distance}**. Set it to 55 mm. Push **OK**.
steps.why: This dimension is for now; the variable size drives it later.
hints: Click the small point at the middle of the circle.
The dialog asks for the distance from the axis.

steps.say: Select the green vertical axis and the front line. Push **{Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceX|Constrain horizontal distance}**. Set it to 75 mm. Push **OK**.
steps.why: The sketch turns green when it has no degrees of freedom left.
hints: The front line is the vertical line near the circle.
The dialog asks for the distance from the axis.

steps.say: Push **{Std_VarSet|Add Variable Set}**. Type **size** in **Name**. Set **Type** to **Length**. Push **OK**.
steps.why: A variable set holds values that dimensions can use.
hints: Find the variable set button in the toolbar.
A dialog asks for the name and the type of the value.

steps.say: Select the variable set in the Model tree. Set **size** to 55 mm in the **Property** view.
hints: The new value is a row in the Property view.
Click the value cell of the size row.
size = 55 mm.

steps.say: Double-click the sketch. Double-click the dimension of the circle place. Push **f(x)**. Type the variable set name, a dot and **size**. Push **OK**.
steps.why: The dimension turns orange: the variable drives it now.
hints: The f(x) button is at the right end of the value box.
An expression names an object, a dot and a property.

steps.say: Double-click the dimension of the front line. Push **f(x)**. Type the variable set name, a dot, **size** and **+ 20 mm**. Push **OK**.
steps.why: The front end stays the same distance from the circle.
hints: Write the unit after the number, or the expression fails.
An expression can add a length to a variable.

steps.why: Pad grows the closed sketch into a solid.
hints: Find Pad in the Part Design toolbar.
The ring shows the button.

steps.why: This is half the width; a mirror makes the other half later.
hints: Find the Length box in the Tasks panel.
The Length box sets how far the sketch grows.
Length = 22 mm.

steps.say: Done: the base of the stem. The Tutor changes size for a moment to check that the part follows it.
